The green bags are not to protect the trunk of the tree. The bags are watering bags that are filled during the growing season with water. The bags were properly installed by the planting contractor to the specifications set forth by the City of Boston Tree Warden. For the BPRD Urban Forestry Division to consider removing a healthy public street tree for this reason, we need proof that the trees roots have caused the damage to the sewer lines. Proof needs to include pictures and invoices from a plumbing contractor which show the sewer line having been repaired and after said repair the trees roots caused new/further damage. Until the documentation is provided and the issue is investigated by the City Arborist the tree cannot be removed as it is protected by state law MGL CH 87. Proof should be sent to 1010 Massachusetts Ave Boston, MA 02118 3rd floor. Attn: Urban Forestry Division or emailed to (Trees@boston.gov) Attn: Urban Forestry Division. It should also be noted that tree roots do not have the ability to break into a sewer pipe. They will however grow into an already broken/compromised sewer pipe. Here is the link to the Boston Water and Sewer Commission, sewer lateral replacement program. https://www.bwsc.org/residential-customers/programs-and-guidelines/sewer-lateral-financial-assistance

We understand and appreciate why seeing the flag flown at half-mast in a timely manner is important, especially during moments of remembrance and respect. Your concern is completely valid, and we appreciate you taking the time to share it with us. Our department is currently responsible for maintaining 217 parks and a significant amount of acreage across the system. With our existing staffing and operational resources, there are times when we are unfortunately unable to lower flags as quickly as we would like. In addition to flag responsibilities, our crews are balancing a wide range of daily and weekly maintenance and safety related tasks across all of the properties we manage. That said, we recognize the importance of this issue and will look at ways to better reallocate our resources and improve our response time when half-mast directives are issued. While there are operational limitations tied to the size and scope of the system we maintain, we are committed to doing our best to address these concerns moving forward.
